holidays.name: National Daiquiri Day
holidays.description: Raise a frosty glass to the classic rum, lime and sugar cocktail. Shake or blend one up, with a strawberry swirl if you like, and toast the sunshine.
holidays.origin: The daiquiri is traditionally linked to Jennings Cox, an American mining engineer working near the Cuban village of Daiquirí around the turn of the 20th century. The story goes that he mixed rum, lime and sugar for guests. The drink then spread from Cuba to bars around the world, and this unofficial day celebrates it.
holidays.funFact: The drink is named after a Cuban mining area and village. John F. Kennedy was reportedly a fan of the cocktail.

holidays.name: Stick Out Your Tongue Day
holidays.description: A day for sticking your tongue out at friends, family and the mirror. It's silly, it's free, and it's a quick stress-buster.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's often tied to the famous 1951 photograph of Albert Einstein sticking out his tongue.
holidays.funFact: Your tongue print is as unique as your fingerprint. Einstein's tongue-out photo was taken on his 72nd birthday, and he liked it enough to order copies for friends.

holidays.name: National Raspberry Cake Day
holidays.description: This is a day to eat cake made with sweet-tart raspberries. Any version counts, including layered, frosted, filled or swirled into a sponge.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the summer berry season and the middle of July's dessert-heavy calendar.
holidays.funFact: A raspberry isn't a single berry. It's a cluster of tiny fruitlets called drupelets, each with its own seed, and one berry can have around 100 of them.
